track: Zero- and low-install ways to deliver the world on the Mac, and giving the agents a GPU
summary:
Choosing Godot does not mean installing a heavy engine on the Mac. Cloud agents can export the macOS app from Linux. The Mac then holds a single arm64 app: 82.9 MB of engine for 4.7.2 (measured), plus the world pack. The owner needs no Godot editor, no Xcode and no Apple Developer account. Milestone 0 (M0) needs two such apps, one per engine version, about 0.2 GB in total. Metal and MoltenVK are both selected by command-line flags, and the benchmark switches are passed the same way. The editor route would instead put 351 MB per unzipped editor on the Mac, plus a 2–6 GB project and import cache.

**Two costs of skipping the editor:**
- Metal shaders cannot be pre-compiled ('baked') from Linux, so the first run stutters while they compile.
- Gatekeeper, macOS's download check, blocks the app if it arrives through a browser. Fetching it with `curl` avoids that.

**The browser** is the only route with nothing to install (Safari on macOS 26 or later). Its costs:
- lower fidelity: lighting scored 5.2 against Godot's 7.0 in the earlier judging;
- no MetalFX upscaling;
- multi-GB tile caches that stay on the internal disk and can be deleted by the browser.

**Godot's web export is the worst option.** It is limited to WebGL2, so SDFGI (Godot's real-time global illumination), SSIL, volumetric fog, auto-exposure, temporal anti-aliasing (TAA) and HDR precision are all lost.

**Streaming** needs 0–60 MB on the Mac, but the GPU rental is a recurring cost.

**Giving agents a GPU.** Only the owner's own Mac gives valid M2 timings.
- **Rented GPU VM:** Remote Control works on Pro and Max. Rates run from about £0.33/h upwards (RunPod L4; I could not open the page to confirm).
- **Claude Code self-hosted environments:** these need a Claude Team plan.
- **GitHub GPU runners:** these need a GitHub Team organisation, at about £2.35/h for a T4.
- **Free GitHub macOS runners:** these expose a virtual GPU on real Metal. That works for WebGPU pages, but Godot's Metal renderer has crashed on it before.

findings.claim: Godot exports for macOS from Linux without a Mac. On non-macOS hosts the default code signing is 'Built-in (ad-hoc only)'. The architecture can be universal, x86_64 or arm64 (arm64 is thinned by Godot's built-in lipo). rcodesign is optional. Notarisation needs a Developer ID certificate and cannot be done with an ad-hoc signature. For owner-only use no Apple Developer account (US$99 a year, reportedly £79 in the UK; unverified) is needed.
findings.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/godotengine/godot/4.7.2-stable/platform/macos/export/export_plugin.cpp (lines 478, 511-513, 553-555, 'Notarization with an ad-hoc signature is not supported'); https://github.com/godotengine/godot-docs/blob/master/tutorials/export/exporting_for_macos.rst

findings.claim:
Measured by HTTP range reads on the official release files:
- The 4.7.2 export-template bundle is 1,281 MB, but its macos.zip is only 123.6 MB. Inside it, godot_macos_release.universal is 170.1 MB, split into an arm64 slice of 82.9 MB and an x86_64 slice of 87.2 MB. The debug build is 186.2 MB. MoltenVK is statically linked (the 'MoltenVK' string is present); there is no separate dylib.
- The 4.8-dev6 bundle is 1,422 MB, with macos.zip at 145.9 MB.
- The web_release.zip template is 10.3 MB.
- The 4.7.2 macOS editor is a 170.6 MB zip that unpacks to a 351.3 MB binary. ENGINE_SELECTION's disk table uses the zip size, not the size on disk.
findings.source: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/releases/tag/4.7.2-stable ; https://github.com/godotengine/godot-builds/releases/tag/4.8-dev6 (templates .tpz and macos.universal.zip, central directories read via Range requests from the container, 23 Sep 2026)

findings.claim: Release export templates accept --rendering-driver, --rendering-method and the '--' separator for user arguments, which the project reads with OS.get_cmdline_user_args(). So one exported app per engine version can run the Metal pass, the MoltenVK pass (--rendering-driver vulkan) and an SDFGI-off pass using a '-- --bench --sdfgi=off' style switch. The owner can skip the Godot editor entirely for the M0 probe: two apps (4.8-dev6 and 4.7.2), about 0.2 GB in total.

Running an app that is ad-hoc signed but not notarised:
- Gatekeeper blocks it only if the app carries the quarantine attribute.
- Apple DTS: 'Most Unix-y tools don't quarantine their downloads, including curl and scp', so an app fetched with curl runs directly. A browser download needs `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine App.app`, or System Settings > Privacy & Security > Open Anyway. Sequoia removed the Control-click Open override.
- Godot warns that an app run from Downloads while quarantined gets path randomisation, which breaks relative paths. Move it out of Downloads first.

Two costs of exporting from Linux:
- **No pre-compiled Metal shaders.** The shader baker (4.5+) on a Linux editor bakes Vulkan shaders only. Metal needs an editor running on macOS, and baking does not work with --headless. An app exported from Linux therefore compiles Metal shaders on first launch (compare the slow-first-load issue #106757), so the M0 bench must discard or repeat the warm-up.
- **Different texture formats.** An arm64 export switches texture formats to ETC2/ASTC, where universal and x86_64 builds use S3TC/BPTC. The Mac build therefore ships differently compressed textures from the ones the cloud (lavapipe) renders use.

WebGPU on the Mac:
- Safari has it on by default only in macOS Tahoe 26 and later.
- Chrome has had it since version 113.
- Firefox has it from 147 on all macOS versions (from 145 on macOS 26+).

The M2 Air is supported by macOS 27 Golden Gate. A zero-install Safari route is therefore possible after an OS update. The owner's current macOS version is unknown.

Browser storage for a streamed world:
- Chromium lets an origin use up to 60% of total disk. WebKit browser apps allow about 60% per origin and 80% across all origins.
- Data is best-effort and is evicted under storage pressure unless navigator.storage.persist() is granted.
- Safari with tracking prevention deletes script-written data from an origin that has had no user interaction for 7 days of browser use.
- The cache lives in the browser profile on the internal disk. Unlike a native app's data pack, it cannot be moved to the external SSD (inference).

Hosting a multi-GB web world:
- **GitHub Pages:** a published site may be no larger than 1 GB, with a 100 GB/month soft bandwidth limit and a 10-minute deploy timeout.
- **Cloudflare R2:** 10 GB-month of storage free, then $0.015 per GB-month. Egress is free, and 10 M Class B reads a month are free. The r2.dev URL is rate-limited and meant for development only, so real use needs a custom domain.
- **GitHub release assets:** a CORS test from the container got no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header, either on github.com's 302 redirect or on the release-assets.githubusercontent.com response. A web viewer therefore cannot fetch releases cross-origin.

Free GitHub macOS runners give real Metal, but not for Godot:
- Standard arm64 macOS runners (macos-latest, M1, 3 vCPU, 7 GB RAM, 14 GB SSD) are free and unlimited for public repositories.
- They expose Metal as an 'Apple Paravirtual device'. Chrome WebGPU and WebGL2 render correctly on it, but it is suitable for checking correctness, not timing.
- Godot's Metal driver crashed on the same device, which reports GPU family Apple5 ('unrecognized selector' in newArgumentEncoderWithLayout, 4.4-beta; the issue is now closed).
- So these runners can give agents free real-Metal appearance renders for a three.js path, but probably not for Godot Forward+ on Metal. MoltenVK on that device is untested.

GitHub GPU and large macOS runners:
- **Linux GPU runner:** 4 CPU, 1 Tesla T4, 28 GB RAM, 16 GB VRAM, 176 GB SSD, running NVIDIA's GPU-Optimized VMI partner image. It costs $0.052/min (about $3.12/h, £2.35/h).
- **macOS xlarge:** M2 Pro, 5 CPU plus 8-core GPU acceleration, $0.102/min (about $6.12/h, £4.61/h).
- **Who can use them:** larger runners are only for organisations on GitHub Team or Enterprise Cloud (Team is $4 per user per month for the first 12 months). They are not free for public repos, included minutes do not apply, minutes are rounded up, and a card and a non-zero spending limit are required.
- **Unknown:** whether headless Vulkan works on the T4 image.

Claude Code on your own GPU:
- **Self-hosted environments** (`claude self-hosted-runner`, which routes cloud sessions to your own hosts) are a public beta for Team and Enterprise organisations only, off by default. Claude Team costs $25 per seat per month billed monthly ($20 annually), with a 2-seat minimum. A standard seat gets about 1.25× Pro usage, which is probably a downgrade from Max.
- **Remote Control**, by contrast, is on Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise. It runs on any machine you run `claude` on, including a remote VM kept alive in tmux, and is driven from claude.ai/code.
- So a rented GPU VM running `claude remote-control` is the route that fits a Pro or Max plan.

Cross-session messaging (Claude Code v2.1.224+) passes plain-text messages between your sessions, through Anthropic's servers when they are on different machines. Messages from other sessions cannot approve permissions or change configuration. So a Claude Code session on the owner's Mac, connected through Remote Control, could run the exported benchmark and send the JSON summary to the cloud session. Whether a cloud session can start that exchange towards the Mac, rather than only reply, is less clear.

Hourly GPU prices, September 2026 (the providers' own pages were blocked by the proxy, so these come from search snippets):
- **RunPod community cloud:** RTX A4000 $0.17/h (about £0.13), L4 $0.44/h (about £0.33), billed per second. Users report the NVIDIA Vulkan driver file missing inside RunPod containers, which is a risk for Godot Forward+.
- **AWS g6.xlarge** (L4, 4 vCPU, 16 GB): $0.8048/h in us-east-1 (about £0.61); London was not retrieved.
- **Scaleway L4-1-24G:** €0.75/h.
- **Hetzner GEX44** (RTX 4000 SFF Ada 20 GB, dedicated): €184 a month, reportedly €234 from August 2026, plus a €79 set-up fee.

To render Godot with Vulkan on a headless NVIDIA server, you need either Xorg on the NVIDIA driver (for example `nvidia-xconfig --use-display-device=None --virtual=...`) or a direct-to-display (DRM) path. Xvfb plus lavapipe will not use the GPU.

Mac-side footprint for streaming: Moonlight 6.1.0's universal macOS DMG is 59.8 MB (measured with an HTTP HEAD request). A WebRTC client in the browser needs 0 MB. No world data is stored on the Mac. Fidelity then depends on the cloud GPU, not the M2 (see the streaming track).
Exchange rate used for the GBP figures: mid-market £1 = $1.3281 on 22 Sep 2026.

verdict:
**Godot survives the 'nothing heavy on the Mac' constraint.** Install size does not disqualify it.

- **What goes on the Mac.** Agents export and ad-hoc sign an arm64 .app in the cloud container. The Mac holds about 83–95 MB of engine per Godot version plus the world pack, and never the editor or its import caches. The world pack is needed by every option except streaming.
- **The M0 probe runs without an editor.** Two exported apps, each run from Terminal, cover it: `--rendering-driver metal` or `--rendering-driver vulkan`, plus `-- --bench`.
- **Two adjustments to milestone 0:**
  - fetch the app with `curl` so Gatekeeper does not block it;
  - treat the first run as a shader warm-up, because Metal shaders cannot be baked from Linux.

**How the other delivery routes compare:**

- **Browser:** the only true zero-install route (Safari on macOS 26+, or Chrome). It costs about 2 lighting points, loses MetalFX, and its tile cache sits on the internal disk and can be evicted by the browser.
- **Godot web export:** strictly dominated. It loses almost the whole lighting stack, so drop it.
- **Cloud streaming:** the only route that beats the M2's ceiling, for 0–60 MB on the Mac. It costs money every hour it runs. UE5 on a cloud GPU needs the owner's explicit OK.

**Giving the agents a GPU, in order of yield:**

1. **Owner's Mac.** Keep lavapipe in the cloud for gate stills, and have the owner run the scripted bench on the Mac per milestone. It is free, and the only source of valid M2 timing and Metal appearance. Results can go back through Claude Code on the Mac with Remote Control, or through a curl upload.
2. **On-demand GPU VM with `claude remote-control`,** only if motion, temporal or streaming checks become necessary. It works on Pro/Max, costs roughly £0.33–0.65/h, and takes 1–3 hours to set up the first time. Prefer a full virtual machine over RunPod containers, because Vulkan is often missing in containers.
3. **Free GitHub macOS runners:** worth it only if the three.js path is chosen.

**Avoid:**
- Claude self-hosted environments: they need the Team plan, a 2-seat minimum and less usage.
- GitHub T4 or M2 Pro runners: they need a Team organisation and cost about £2.35–4.61/h. Nothing about them beats a VM, and their virtual GPUs cannot give M2 timing.
costs:
All GBP figures use £1 = $1.328 and exclude VAT unless stated.

**Delivery options**
- **Godot exported app:** £0. Code signing needs no Apple account. Notarisation would need the Apple Developer Program at $99 a year (reportedly £79 in the UK, unverified), which is not needed for owner-only use.
- **Browser build hosting:**
  - Cloudflare R2 is free up to 10 GB-month; a 20 GB world costs about $0.15 a month. Egress is £0.
  - A custom domain costs about £10 a year (unverified).
  - GitHub Pages is free but capped at 1 GB.
- **Streaming:** the client is free; GPU rental is covered by the streaming track.

**Agent GPU options**
- **Owner's Mac:** £0, plus about 15 minutes of owner time per run.
- **GitHub macOS standard runner:** £0 on a public repo. It gives real Metal appearance for WebGPU, not for Godot.
- **GitHub Linux T4:** $0.052/min, about £2.35/h. It also needs a GitHub Team organisation at $4 (about £3) per user per month.
- **GitHub macOS xlarge (M2 Pro):** $0.102/min, about £4.61/h, with the same Team requirement.
- **RunPod:** L4 $0.44/h (about £0.33), A4000 $0.17/h (about £0.13), community cloud, per-second billing. Unverified, and Vulkan may be missing in its containers.
- **AWS g6.xlarge (L4):** $0.8048/h in us-east-1 (about £0.61); London is probably dearer (unverified).
- **Scaleway L4:** €0.75/h (about £0.65, unverified exchange rate).
- **Hetzner GEX44:** €184–234 a month (about £160–205) plus a €79 set-up fee. Worth it only above roughly 250–400 GPU-hours a month.
- **Claude self-hosted environments:** need Claude Team at 2 × $25 a month (about £38, plus VAT), probably with less usage than Max. Not recommended.

**Scenario: 20 GPU-hours a month for agent renders**
- RunPod L4: about £7
- AWS L4: about £12
- GitHub T4: about £47 plus £3 for the Team plan
- Hetzner: about £160–205 flat
- Owner's Mac: £0
mac_footprint:
Disk on the Mac and what the owner has to do by hand, per option (sizes marked 'est.' are estimates):

**(a) Godot app exported by cloud agents, no editor**
- **Disk:**
  - about 83 MB of engine per app for 4.7.2 (arm64 slice, measured), probably about 90–95 MB for 4.8-dev6;
  - the M0 probe needs 2 apps, about 0.2 GB, plus a tiny probe pack;
  - the full world pack is 2–5 GB (est.) and can sit on an external SSD;
  - the Metal shader cache is a few hundred MB (est.);
  - no project folder and no `.godot` import cache on the Mac.
- **Compared with the editor route:** 351 MB per unzipped editor (0.7 GB for both versions) plus a 2–6 GB project cache.
- **By hand:** paste one Terminal command that downloads with `curl`, unzips and runs the `--bench` passes, about 12 minutes each. Then return the JSON, either through Claude Code on the Mac or a `curl` upload. If the app came through a browser, run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine` or click Open Anyway. No Xcode, no Apple account.

**(b) Browser build (three.js, Babylon or PlayCanvas, including splats)**
- **Disk:**
  - 0 MB to install with Safari on macOS 26+; otherwise Chrome (size unverified) or Firefox 147+;
  - world cache 0–5 GB inside the browser profile on the internal disk. It cannot be moved, and it can be evicted unless storage persistence is granted.
- **By hand:** open a URL. Possibly update macOS first; the OS update's temporary disk need is unverified. One-off hosting set-up: a Cloudflare account, an R2 bucket and a custom domain, or GitHub Pages if the world stays under 1 GB.

**(c) Godot web export**
- **Disk:** the same as (b), plus about 10 MB of engine (the web template).
- **Fidelity:** lowest of all four; not recommended.

**(d) Streaming from a cloud GPU**
- **Disk:** 0 MB with a browser WebRTC client, or 59.8 MB for Moonlight. No world data on the Mac.
- **By hand:** a provider account and card, then start and stop the instance each session. UE5 needs the owner's explicit OK.

**Giving the agents a GPU**
- **Owner's Mac:** nothing extra to install, assuming Claude Code and git are already there from the UE5 work (unverified).
- **GPU VM:** nothing on the Mac. Setting up the VM takes 1–3 hours the first time: account, card, NVIDIA driver, headless Xorg or Vulkan, Claude Code and a `claude remote-control` login.
- **GitHub GPU runners:** create an organisation, buy the Team plan, and set up billing and a spending limit.
unknowns: The owner's macOS version, which decides whether Safari has WebGPU, and whether git and Xcode Command Line Tools are already installed.
Whether Godot 4.8-dev6 or 4.7.2 now fails gracefully or runs under MoltenVK on GitHub's paravirtual Metal device (Apple5). One free workflow run would settle it.
Whether headless Vulkan works for Godot Forward+ on GitHub's T4 partner image and on RunPod, Scaleway or AWS images without extra driver work.
Whether a claude.ai/code cloud session can start a message to a Remote Control session on the owner's Mac, or only reply to one.
The exact arm64 slice size of the 4.8-dev6 release template. I did not extract it; about 90–95 MB is inferred from macos.zip being 145.9 MB.
The Metal shader cache size and first-run compile time for an app exported from Linux without baked shaders, on this M2.
Current prices on RunPod, Scaleway, Hetzner and Lambda, and AWS London prices. Their pages were blocked by the container proxy, so I used search snippets.
Chrome's installed size on macOS in 2026, and the temporary disk space a macOS 26/27 update needs on a 256 GB Air.
Whether Godot handles very large .pck files (more than 4 GB) cleanly for the full world, or whether it should be split into several packs.
